blocks.html: At the end of every term, a class teacher prepares report cards. For each student, the teacher adds the marks of five subjects, finds the percentage, decides the grade and the result, and finally finds the class topper, the class average and how many students passed. Doing this by hand for 60 students takes hours and mistakes are common.
Our task: write a C++ program that does all of this automatically.

items.html: Each student has marks in 5 subjects, each out of 100.
Marks must be between 0 and 100; any other value must be rejected and asked again.
A student fails if he or she scores below 33 in any subject, even if the percentage is high.
Grades by percentage: A1 90 and above, A2 75–89.99, B 60–74.99, C 45–59.99, D 33– 44.99, E below 33.
At the end, print the number of students, number passed, pass percentage, class average percentage and the topper.

rows: A report card for each student
Grade by else-if ladder; result PASS/FAIL
Keep count of passes, sum of percentages and highest percentage

blocks.html: Why does topPercent start at −1? Every real percentage is 0 or more, so the first student is always greater than −1 and becomes the first "topper so far". Each later student replaces the topper only if he or she scores higher.
